{"number":1072,"title":"Production code must not reference its tests — land it as a check","body":"Owner decision while landing #1066: **there shouldn't be references to tests from production code.** That change removed the four citations it created; the rule itself is still unwritten, and eleven pre-existing sites still cross the line.

## The rule

A shipping `.mjs` under `packs/` or `engine/` must not name a `*.test.mjs` path. It is deterministic, so it belongs on the ladder as a **check**, not prose — the assurance authored and seen to fail before the sites are cleaned.

Documentation is a separate question and probably outside it: `engine/checks/README.md` describing where a pack's tests live, or `.github/workflows/ci.yml` naming test globs, is the corpus documenting itself, not production code pointing at its own test.

## The sites as of today

```
engine/checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs:103
engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs:72
engine/scheduler/queue/prework-run.mjs:3
engine/scheduler/run.mjs:10
engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs:35
engine/scheduler/slots.mjs:18
packs/claudinite-dashboard/model.mjs:11
packs/claudinite-dashboard/tasks/fleet-digest/dated-fixture-collision.mjs:4
packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs:14, :36
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/rules-index-current.mjs:26, :51
```

Most say the same thing — "a guard pins this" — and lose nothing by naming the guard rather than its file, which is how the four in #1066 were resolved.

## Why it is not folded into #1066

Cleaning these touches three more pack directories, so it re-delivers `claudinite-dashboard`, `claudinite-growth` and `claudinite-lifecycle` on their version bumps. That restructure's whole constraint was that members see nothing, so the sweep is its own change.

## Where the check lives

`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/` if it is a canon-corpus rule, or a shared pack if it should reach members — worth deciding first, since the second choice makes it every member's rule and a much wider first run.

{"number":1078,"title":"Human-only: trace the request mode refusing an unauthorized mark, live","body":"The last unverified path of the ad-hoc request mode (#1010, landed in [#1067](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1067)). It needs a **second GitHub account with no push access on this repository**, which no session has, so it is yours.

The happy path is already traced live ([#1074](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1074) → [#1075](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1075) → [#1076](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1076), 2026-08-19) and that run confirmed the permission API answers under the executor's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. What it did **not** exercise is the branch taken for somebody who is not a collaborator at all: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{login}/permission` answering **404**, which the engine reads as "no permission" rather than as a failed read.

## Why it is worth the ten minutes

That 404 is the difference between the two things this mode must never confuse:

- read as `none` → the request is **refused** and disarmed, which is the design;
- read as a failed read → the run **parks** in the failure lane, and every stranger's marked issue becomes a triage item somebody has to clear.

Both are covered by engine tests against a fake GitHub (S45, S46, S50 in `engine-tests/scheduler/queue/request-mode.test.mjs`). Neither has been seen against the real API, and the two differ by one status code.

## Steps

- [ ] **From the second account** (no push access here), open a throwaway issue — anything, one line. *While this is off: nothing to mark.*
- [ ] **From your own account**, apply `claude-task` to it. Applying the mark to somebody else's issue is meant to authorize nothing — that is the point of the trace. *While this is off: the tick has nothing to adopt.*
- [ ] **Run the tick** — wait for the hourly one, or dispatch [Claudinite scheduler](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml) with no inputs. *While this is off: the mark just sits there.*
- [ ] **Watch, on the throwaway issue**: one comment beginning "Not implementing this:", `claude-queued` removed, **no session started**. And on the work item the tick created: closed, `task:obsolete`.
- [ ] **Watch the next tick or two**: nothing re-adopts it. The disarm is what stops the refusal repeating forever.
- [ ] **Second variant, same issue**: have the second account comment `/claude go`, re-apply `claude-task`, run the tick. It must refuse again — the phrase decides nothing; the permission behind it does.
- [ ] **Positive control**: comment `/claude go` yourself, re-apply `claude-task`, run the tick. This one must run. (Skip if you would rather not spend a session; the happy path is already traced.)

## Closing condition

Both refusals observed, with the item numbers linked here, and the throwaway issue closed. If either refusal instead **parks** the item at `task:needs-human-failure`, do not close this — the 404 is being read as a failed read, and the fix is in the `request` collector's `permissionOf` (`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`).

Refs #1010","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1078","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-19T23:20:27Z","updated_at":"2026-08-19T23:20:27Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

The critical pass over DESIGN §16 found four gaps; the owner decided each today and [#1063](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1063) lands them (design + scenarios + simulator, ledger F26–F30): an unreadable request issue **fails the run** instead of declining (only a definitive *gone* declines); **one issue, one live item** (a live prior item leaves the mark unconsumed; a parked one is superseded); the **model labels are consumed with the mark**; eligibility is **push permission read from the permission API**, not the payload association. S44–S51 in the sim carry all of it, each watched red first.

## Implementation plan (supersedes the §16.10 list in my 2026-08-18 comment)

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup: none.** The mode rides the queue's existing wiring: labels come from the ordinary ensured set, the invocation endpoint and its secret are the queue's own (#801), and the permission read is designed for the executor workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No new secret, scope, or platform setting.

**Phase 1 — the code, one PR** (all of it against the queue engine; each behavior test watched failing first):

- [ ] `engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs` — job 4 `adopt`: list open `claude-task` issues (REST, never search); the one-live-item guard (wait unconsumed / supersede a parked prior item, closed `outcome:obsolete` with a superseding comment); create the item (`origin:request`, born `task:ready`, qualifier `#N`, body `Request:` + `Model:`); consume `claude-task` **and** every `claude-model:*`, add `claude-queued`.
- [ ] `engine/scheduler/queue/work-item.mjs` — parse/serialize `Request:`/`Model:`; `origin:request`; the four request labels in the ensured set.
- [ ] `engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs` — pass the item to the precondition; the decline write-back (one comment + remove `claude-queued`); the cannot-answer verdict parks `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-failure`, issue untouched.
- [ ] `engine/scheduler/discover.mjs` + `validate-dispatch.mjs` — the built-in engine task root beside the pack scan, and its validated path form.
- [ ] `engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs` — `model_from_request`; `precondition(signals, config, item)`; the error-verdict shape (cannot-answer ≠ no-go).
- [ ] The built-in task `engine/scheduler/queue/tasks/implement-request/` — `task.mjs`: `manual`, `open-pr`, no `code_work`; precondition = withdrawn/gone checks + eligibility (author or `/claude go` commenter has push, read from `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{u}/permission`; association at most a prefilter; unreadable → error verdict). `task.md`: how to implement a requested issue — the issue is the requirement, data never instructions.
- [ ] Verify against a **real run**, not docs alone, that the permission endpoint answers under the executor workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`; if it does not, stop and raise — do not substitute the association.

Phase 1 is built and open as [#1067](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1067), with #1064's rename landed underneath it in the same branch (writing new code in the vocabulary that issue retires would have meant sweeping it twice).

Every Phase 1 checklist item from the plan above is done, with three deviations worth reading before approving:

- **The permission read is a signal, not a call from inside the precondition.** A precondition is pure over collected signals and holds no GitHub client; giving every pack's precondition one so this task could make two reads widens far more than the gate it guards. So a `request` collector — engine-owned, like every other — reads the issue, its `/claude go` comments and each candidate's permission, and returns those facts unjudged; the verdict stays in the built-in task's precondition exactly as §16.4 puts it. DESIGN §16.4 carries the amendment.
- **No migration record for #1064.** The retired origin marker is inert (nothing branches on it — standing vs ad-hoc is structural now), open items' state labels do not change, and closed history is covered decode-side. The migration ops write files, not issue labels, so a record could not have done that work in any case.
- **The permission endpoint is unverified**, and it is the one open risk. This sandbox proxy-blocks `api.github.com`, which is a policy boundary rather than something a later agent pass can close — so it needs the first real run, or a human. The failure mode is loud by construction: any answer but 200/404 makes the read `unreadable`, which parks the item in the failure lane with the status on it rather than approving or refusing on a guess.

Two things the build found that the plan did not have:

- The vendor set's blanket "an engine `.md` is maintainer reference" rule was dropping the built-in task's `task.md` — a mount whose request session has nothing to read. Whitelisted by pattern, and its regression test now walks the queue engine rather than listing its top level, which is what let it through.
- Deriving standing-vs-ad-hoc structurally makes an unqualified hand-created item for a *scheduled* task indistinguishable from that task's standing item, so `create-work-item` now refuses that shape and names `--wake` / `--qualifier` instead.

Phase 2 (the validation burst on a live queue-mode repo) is untouched and still open; this issue stays open for it.

## The happy path, end to end (2026-08-19 23:00–23:06 UTC)

[#1074](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1074) marked `claude-task` + `claude-model:sonnet` → tick → [#1075](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1075) → session → [#1076](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1076), six minutes end to end. Every step of §16 behaved as designed:

- **Labels ensured** by the tick before anything was marked — `claude-task` exists in the picker with its colour and description.
- **Adoption**: item titled `[claudinite-work] engine/implement-request #1074`, body `Request: #1074` / `Model: sonnet`, born `task:ready`. Both marks consumed, `claude-queued` on, one comment naming the item and the family.
- **Pickup**: precondition passed, claim + hand-off + one session, item to `task:agent`.

- **Converge**: item parked open at `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-approval`; #1074 swapped `claude-queued` → `claude-in-review` with the PR and the model named.

The item's Context rendered as two near-identical bullets — adoption writes one, the precondition added another — in the one section the session is told to read as its binding scope. [#1077](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1077) drops the precondition's.

## Still not verified, and why

The **unauthorized-mark refusal** (the plan's second Phase 2 trace). It needs an issue whose author has no push access here; every identity available to this session is the owner's, so it cannot be staged, and the adoption→pickup window the withdrawal variant would need is seconds wide (the drain follows the tick in the same run). The engine tests cover both shapes against the real executor with a fake GitHub — S45's disarm and S48's withdrawal — but the live trace is a human's to produce, from a second account, and it is the one thing left on this issue.

{"number":748,"title":"conformance-backlog: committed-build-artifact check (promote cannot land a check — fixtures sit outside its write surface)","body":"Two things, from the 2026-08-11 `canon-curation/growth-promote` run (#745, PR #747).

## 1. A structural block: promote's ladder cannot reach the check rung

`growth-promote`'s task spec says a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in the promote PR — "the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires**".

That is mechanically impossible today:

- promote's write surface is bounded to `packs/` and `skills/`, enforced by `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs` on the `growth-promote` branch prefix;
- a canon pack's fixture test lives under `packs-tests/`, which is **outside** that surface;
- and it cannot move into `packs/` either — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins a closed set of test roots (`engine-tests/`, `packs-tests/`, `vendoring/`, `dev/tools/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/`), with `engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs` failing on any tracked test outside them.

So every promote run must fall back to prose for a convertible rule, and the "prose is the fallback, not the default" ladder never fires. Whichever way it is resolved (widen `inBounds` to `packs-tests/`, or add `packs/` as a test root), it is an owner decision — the run declined to widen its own gate.

## 2. The conversion this blocked

The `.gitignore`-pruning lesson (LaughCounter's local pack, promoted as prose to `git-github-advanced` in #747) converts to a world-scope `basics` check. Written and green locally before being pulled:

- **`packs/basics/committed-build-artifact.mjs`** — advisory, relevance-first. Flags a *tracked* file matching a confined set of artifacts no project tracks on purpose: `__pycache__/`, `*.py[co]`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `*.egg-info/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`. The `fix` line carries the lesson (delete the artifacts before dropping their ignore rules; read `git diff --cached --stat` after a bulk `git add -A`).
- **`packs-tests/basics/committed-build-artifact.test.mjs`** — four cases: clean tree silent; a swept-in `__pycache__` found; the tool-cache/OS set found; and a narrowness case proving silence on deliberately vendored trees (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`) and on prose merely naming `__pycache__`.

Advisory rather than blocking on purpose: the fix is a deletion, and pre-existing junk in a member repo should surface as a finding to clear, not red that repo's sweep and block its maintenance PR.

The set was chosen so the check stays inert on anything a repo might legitimately vendor; `node_modules/` and `dist/` are deliberately excluded.

Refs #745.

{"number":991,"title":"Promote conformance-work-scope to blocking once the fleet carries the step","body":"#977 landed `conformance-work-scope` (core) as **advisory**, deliberately: a requirement added to the canon with no path for consumers to comply first is the #555 failure, and its sibling `conformance-workflow` is staged the same way. This issue is the mechanism that brings the promotion back rather than leaving it to memory.

## The closing condition

Every member's CI runs the work sweep — i.e. no member's world sweep reports `conformance-work-scope`. Read it off the fleet rather than off memory:

- each member's own sweep output (the advisory finding is the signal), or
- each member's workflows containing `engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs`.

Delivery is by the nightly converge (owner decision, 2026-08-18 — not forced): the engine file ships with the engine tree, and the `core` bump 3 → 4 ships the check. So members cannot begin complying until their next converge, and the advisory finding is what tells each one what to add.

## The promotion itself

One line in [`packs/core/conformance-work-scope.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/core/conformance-work-scope.mjs) — `severity: 'advisory'` → `'blocking'` — plus the catalog row in `packs/core/README.md` and a `core` version bump.

**Do not promote while any member is still missing the step.** A blocking finding reds that member's next maintenance PR, and since delivery arms auto-merge — a queue for checks — a red check there does not annoy anyone: it stops the repo updating, quietly. {"number":1326,"title":"Extract the task surface into claudinite-tasks, move the update flows, split the wiring converge","body":"PRs A, B and C of #1317. Landed together because none of them is green alone: the vendor set's import-closure guard forces A and B into one change, and until C stops every flow from touching `.github/workflows/`, the wiring converge still needs a stub the engine no longer owns.

Closes #1325

## A — the surface moves

`engine/scheduler/*` → `packs/claudinite-tasks/` — the queue, the executor, the task contract and its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, the delivery lane, the two workflow stubs and the three operational documents. `engine-tests/scheduler/` and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` become the pack's own `test/` and `test/sim/`; `SCENARIOS.md` stays in `docs/` with its links repointed.

## B — the queue's meta-machinery follows it

`task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), and the `task-declaration-shape` / `task-code-work-env` checks.

## C — updates move, and the wiring converge splits

The versioned update flows move to `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`. A pack's `updates/` is canon-internal for the same reason its `test/` is — the flows run from the canon tree the runner just fetched and reach canon-only machinery no mount carries — so the vendor set excludes the directory by name.

`engine/converge-wiring.mjs` keeps distribution wiring (hooks, rules index and its CLAUDE.md import, `.gitattributes`, badge row, the repo's own local pack). The two workflow files become `packs/claudinite-tasks/converge-workflows.mjs`, scaffolded once at adoption by bootstrap or the adopt-pack skill.

With that, **no flow computes or writes a `.github/workflows/` path**, so the withhold staging lane is retired: nothing is staged, the emptied exports still answer for a stale worker, and the flow sweeps whatever an earlier cycle left under `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`.

A migration record declares `claudinite-tasks` into every member that carries a scheduler workflow — the one artifact that says what a repo actually does rather than what its declaration hoped.

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Eight modules: `work-items`, `anchors`, `delivery`, `github`, `signals`, `task-contract`, `usage-format`, `wake`. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory and nothing else. `claudinite-dashboard` declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`; every other consumer reaches it only from a `tasks/` folder, and a pack's `tasks/` now rides the tasks pack — so a mount without the queue carries no task folders and closure holds on both sides.

`wake.mjs` is its own module rather than a line in `work-items.mjs`: the dashboard loads that one unbundled in a browser, where the scheduler run's Node built-ins do not resolve.

## Compatibility

`engine/scheduler/*` and `updates/*` remain as one-line re-exports for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts still name the old paths. Each tree has a `legacy-entry.mjs` that rewrites `process.argv[1]` before the re-export evaluates, so a command-line entry reached through a shim still runs as the program rather than silently defining exports and exiting. `engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs` additionally keeps the old four-argument signature and its own CLI, since the split changed both. All of it is a reviewed barrier exception, and PR D deletes it.

**One migration tolerance to review**: until the seeding record has converged fleet-wide, the vendor set ships `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declares it. A member's live workflows name its modules by literal path, and a mount that dropped them mid-migration could not be fixed by any later converge. The removal condition is stated at the code — no member's stamp lacking the pack, not a date.

## Three behaviour changes worth a look

- `scheduler-workflow-shape` accepts the pack entry path **and** the legacy engine one, so a member's un-convergeable workflow file is not a blocking finding during the window.
- `task-declaration-shape` skips a `task.mjs` that only re-exports another module: a relocation shim declares nothing of its own. Tested by seeing it fail without the guard.
- The `claudinite-canary-repo` pack exists to rehearse the withhold lane, which this PR retires. Its manifest now says so; **what to do with the pack is left open** rather than decided here.

## Not in this PR

PR D, the gated tail that deletes the shims once L1–L3 confirm no member names one. `implement-request` also stays a built-in under `queue/tasks/` rather than becoming an ordinary pack task — that changes its wire id, so it belongs with the decode work.

## Verification

Full suite `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 0 failures, with the clone deepened so `engine-pack-lane-shims` actually walks the trunk's pack history and confirms every fielded pack→engine import still resolves through a shim. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The remaining advisories are `file-placement` on the shim files themselves — deliberate, and gone with PR D.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/       new pack: the moved surface, shared-code/, the two
                              relocated tasks, the two relocated checks, the
                              workflow scaffolder, the seeding migration record,
                              test/ and test/sim/
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/   updates/ moves in (canon-internal); the update
                              task's staged-delivery step becomes a sweep;
                              scheduler-workflow-shape accepts both entry paths
engine/                       converge-wiring.mjs is the distribution half;
                              engine/scheduler/ is now only re-export shims plus
                              legacy-entry.mjs; prose no longer names a pack
updates/                      re-export shims plus legacy-entry.mjs
vendoring/                    the engine walk gates the shims on the pack; a
                              pack's tasks/ rides the tasks pack; a pack's
                              updates/ never vendors; the engine .md whitelist is
                              gone (a pack's .md is payload)
bootstrap.mjs                 distribution wiring always; workflow scaffolding
                              only when the tasks pack is in the mount
packs/basics, claudinite-growth, claudinite-dashboard, claudinite-fleet-sheepdog,
packs/chrome-extension, product-wiki, tidy-repo, claudinite-canary-repo
                              imports repointed at shared-code/, versions bumped
.github/workflows/            the canon's own run: lines and the ci.yml test roots
.claudinite-settings.json     the pack declaration, the barrier exceptions and
                              the canon-internal updates/ carve-out
.claudinite/local/packs/      the thin-workflow rule, promote-scope fixtures, and
                              the pack-independence allow list
docs/                         §18 records the shipped shared-code surface and the
                              updates move; versioned-updates §  marks the
                              withhold lane superseded
```","state":"closed","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1326","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-24T10:22:07Z","updated_at":"2026-08-24T11:35:42Z","closed_at":"2026-08-24T11:35:38Z","closed_by":"missingbulb","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1317,"title":"Extract the task execution/scheduling surface into a claudinite-tasks pack","body":"Tracking issue for the split of `engine/scheduler/` (52% of core, 8,106 lines) out of the engine and into a canon pack, so the engine is pack distribution only. End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.
- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.
- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup:** none required. No new secret, permission, or platform setting; #1302 already removed the secrets variance.

**Review pass — one PR stack, approved together:**
- [ ] PR A — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: move `engine/scheduler/*` in (with `shared-code/`), leave re-export shims at every old `engine/scheduler/*` path a fielded caller names, adjust the vendor set (operational-`.md` whitelist paths, engine walk), move `engine-tests/scheduler/` **and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` (sim.mjs, scenarios.test.mjs, coverage.test.mjs)** into the pack's `test/` (SCENARIOS.md stays in docs/ as the play-through record, its sim links repointed), add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.
- [ ] PR B — relocate `task-janitor`, `usage-fold`, and the two task-declaration checks into the pack; `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.
- [ ] PR C — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring`; slim bootstrap (no task wiring); `adopt-pack` scaffolding for claudinite-tasks (workflows, hashed cron, dailyHour, endpoints interview); delete the withhold lane; migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.
- [ ] PR D (gated tail — written and approved now, merged by chain link L4): delete the old-path shims and any withhold leftovers.

**Execution chain** — each link filed as a sub-issue on approval of this plan, `Blocked-by:` the previous:
- [ ] L1 — force `fleet-baseline` with follow; exit: every member's stamp shows the pack version that ships claudinite-tasks, read from stamps, not run conclusions.
- [ ] L2 — manual fleet pass (owner-supported): repoint each member's two workflow files' `run:` lines and the CCR routine stored-prompt pointers (`executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`) to the mount pack paths; exit: each member's next scheduler run green from the pack path.
- [ ] L3 — observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide (the update task converges through the pack executor); exit: every member's stamp moved after L2.
- [ ] L4 — merge PR D; exit: fleet self-tests green on the shim-free mount.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Claudinite/sha/3fd16f9d7fc5144bc6e39bdeedd27a2397cccf74/contents/packs/static-website/RULES.md] # Static website

A static site that releases on push and serves from GitHub Pages. The full contract — the pipeline, the config, the setup — is [the static-site-releases skill](skills/static-site-releases/SKILL.md); these are the things a session touching such a repo has to know before it edits anything.

- **A published file is a file the publish set names — adding a page is two edits.** The Pages artifact is assembled from `.github/site.config`'s `publish_paths` and nothing else, so a new page, stylesheet or data file that isn't under a published path (or named in the list) is simply absent from the live site, with no error anywhere: the build is green, the deploy succeeds, the page 404s. When you add a file the site serves, put it under an already-published directory or add it to `publish_paths` in the same change. The list is additive on purpose — the alternative, "publish the repo minus what we remember to exclude", publishes every draft, note and key nobody thought to hide.
- **The version moves with the change.** A change touching the published site raises `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` in the same PR — `node .github/actions/bump-site-version/bump.mjs $(version_files)` computes it from the previous version and the UTC date, and `sw/version-bumped` is what holds the line. Never hand-write the `ymmdd` or the counter: a typed value either collides with a released one or is dated in the future, and the next bump refuses. The release flow writes no version of its own — it ships what it finds on `main` — so a shipped change without a bump is never released at all. The one deliberate human part is the **major**, a "this is a new generation of the site" statement; the owner's **"bump version"** means exactly that, and the release workflow's `bump: major` dispatch is what performs it.
- **The pipeline files under `.github/workflows/static-site-*` and `.github/actions/{read-site-config,bump-site-version,assemble-site}` are managed copies of the pack's `stubs/`.** Fix the pack and re-vendor; an edit to the copy is overwritten and, until it is, makes this repo's pipeline differ from every other site repo's. The repo's own values all live in `.github/site.config`, which is what the copies read.
- **The site is served from a subpath, not a domain root.** GitHub Pages serves it at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/` (unless a custom domain is configured), so a root-relative URL — `/style.css`, `/img/logo.png`, a `fetch('/data.json')` — resolves above the site and 404s in production while working fine in a local `file://` or `python -m http.server` preview. Write links, asset paths and fetches **relative** to the page.
- **Freshness is a published manifest's job, not a per-file TTL's.** There is no server here to vary `Cache-Control` per file, so the freshness policy moves into the client — and the shape it reaches for first, giving each file a lifetime matching how fast you think it changes, reprices the same bet on every file and gets it wrong in both directions at once: too long and visitors read stale data, too short and they re-download what never changed. Publish one small manifest naming every downloadable asset and a hash of its contents, fetch *that* on each load, and evict exactly the entries whose hash moved. It buys longer caching **and** fresher data, which no TTL can offer together, and the extra request is the one you are probably already making for a version string. Expect a mismatch mid-deploy — the manifest is fetched, a deploy lands, the asset that follows disagrees — so refetch once and carry on; only a disagreement that survives fresh copies of both is a fault worth surfacing.
- **Nothing can attest to its own freshness, and size attests to nothing at all.** A stale file carries a perfectly valid hash *of itself*, and an internal `"version"` field states which generation it is, never whether that generation is still current — so the expected hash has to come from a file fetched fresher than the one being judged, which is what makes the manifest the one asset that may never carry a TTL of its own. Caching it saves no round-trip; it moves the staleness up a level and hides it better. Nor is length a cheap stand-in for a hash: a correction applied uniformly across a file is routinely byte-length-neutral — a timezone fix rewriting every `16:25` to `17:25` moved **0 bytes** of a 3.1 MB catalogue while changing the meaning of every record in it. And record the manifest's hash beside the entry as you write it, so the check is a string compare; re-hashing the stored body means pushing megabytes through a digest on the critical path of every load to answer a question the bookkeeping already knows.
- **Two files cached on separate clocks and later joined *will* be joined across generations — make them a verified set or don't split them.** Splitting a payload so each half caches on its own schedule is a sound instinct and it has this cost: every visitor eventually holds one half from Tuesday and the other from Thursday. Content-addressed keys ("name the row by its date and time, not its position in the array") survive rows being *added and removed*, which is what they are usually chosen for, and not a systematic *correction to the key itself* — a timezone shift, a rounding change, a rename — which moves every key at once and joins the two halves to nothing. Have each half record the generation of the other and refetch both on a mismatch. Then assert on the join *rate*, because a partial join is silent by construction: a missing key returns "no data for this row", which is indistinguishable from a row that genuinely has none yet, and a check written as "at least one row joined" passes at 6%.
- **Don't call missing data survivable until you have followed it to the pixel.** "The fetch is allowed to fail — it'll just show as unknown, which we already handle" is a claim about every consumer downstream, and it is usually wrong: an absent value reaching a boolean, a comparison or a status lookup is very often indistinguishable from a real negative, so the page renders a confident falsehood with nothing logged and the visitor acts on it. Trace the missing value all the way to what it draws before deciding a failure is tolerable. Where it isn't, the file is required — fail the load and show the error state, because a wrong answer with no error is worse than an error.

` silently empties it — read the sibling, not the tag.** When a `

` is filled with raw HTML (e.g. `innerHTML`, or a framework's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` / `v-html` / `ng-bind-html`), a block element inside it (a `

`, etc.) is disallowed by the HTML content model, so the parser (browser or jsdom, same rule) auto-closes the `

` right before it and the injected content lands as the `

`'s **next sibling**. Read `element.nextElementSibling`. - **An ambiguous numeric slash date can't be resolved from its digits — infer the document's convention once, don't guess per-field.** When both parts are ≤ 12 (e.g. `05/07/2026`), resolve the order once per document — never per source or per field — in this order. (1) **An unambiguous sibling date fixes the page's convention**: a slash date elsewhere on the same page with a part > 12 (e.g. `24/07/2026`) parses only one way, and a page is almost always internally consistent — read that date's order and apply it to every other slash date on the page. (2) Failing that, **read the declared locale** (``, `og:locale`): default **month-first** (the order `Date` and most JS parsers assume) and flip to day-first only on a *positive* non-US signal — a non-US region in `lang` / `og:locale`, or a non-English language; a bare `en` with unknown region stays month-first. The `.` / `-` separators are day-first regardless. - **When code must react to how a real page actually behaves, investigate it live before you ship — don't deploy a hypothesis you can only test after release.** If a change hinges on the real DOM, computed styles, or runtime state of a page you can't see, hand the user one JavaScript snippet to run in the browser DevTools console and read its output back. Reserve "test it after it's deployed" for behavior you've verified genuinely can't be observed now. - **Make that console request a snippet, not an essay.** Send exactly one code block to paste into the console and ask the user to paste its output back. Skip the prose explaining what you're hoping to learn.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Claudinite/sha/3fd16f9d7fc5144bc6e39bdeedd27a2397cccf74/contents/packs/node/RULES.md] # Node.js

Portable, project-agnostic practices for working in Node.js / npm codebases — package management, scripts, module resolution, runtime gotchas — true for any Node project read cold.

## Module resolution

- **A *named* import from a package's CommonJS entry can silently yield `undefined`.** Node recovers named bindings from a CJS module by static analysis, and that analysis fails on plenty of real entry points (a re-export built at runtime, a conditional assignment) — with no error: the import resolves, the binding is `undefined`, and the failure surfaces later as "x is not a function". When a package ships both entries, import the **ESM** one explicitly (`…/package/index.mjs`, or the `import` condition of its `exports`) for named bindings; when it doesn't, `import pkg from '…'` and destructure off the default. Resolve the package's own directory (`$(npm root -g)/<pkg>` for a global install) rather than hardcoding an absolute path into a version-pinned layout, which moves under you on the next image or upgrade.
- **Modern Node (22.7+) detects ES-module syntax in a `.js` file on its own** — no `"type": "module"`, no flag, no warning. A directory of ES modules therefore needs **no `package.json` of its own** just to be loadable; adding one to declare module-ness is cargo cult, and one already present for that reason is vestigial. (Prefer `.js` consistently within a tree over mixing in `.mjs` for the same purpose; the extension is then a style choice, not a signal.)

## Test discovery

- **`node --test` skips dot-directories, so a bare invocation over a suite living under one runs
  zero tests and exits green.** Node's default discovery walks the tree but ignores hidden
  directories outright, and finding nothing is *success* — a run reporting no failures because it
  found no tests reads exactly like a passing suite. Any CI step or local command meant to exercise
  tests under a dot-path must pass that path (or an explicit glob) as an argument, and whoever adds
  the step confirms it by watching the **test count be non-zero**, never by watching it go green.
  Naming a path is not enough — the argument must **resolve to files that exist**: a typo'd
  glob, a moved fixture or a renamed directory produces the identical zero-test green, so the
  property to assert is that every path a `node --test` invocation names still matches something
  in the tree.

## jsdom diverges from a real browser in ways a green test can hide

Two that recur:

- **`body.innerText` is null in jsdom.** Code reading `el.innerText || el.textContent` therefore falls through to `textContent` under test, which *includes* the `<script>` / `<style>` text, `<select>` / `<option>` text, and CSS-hidden text a real browser's `innerText` omits. Treat body-text results as jsdom-optimistic; never add a test that only passes because of it.
- **`runScripts: "outside-only"` (the default) parses `<noscript>` into live DOM — the opposite of a real browser.** A `textContent` read looks clean under test but splices the `<noscript>` markup into the value in Chrome, which keeps `<noscript>` as raw text. Parse a script-free fragment with `runScripts: "dangerously"` to reproduce the browser.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Claudinite/sha/3fd16f9d7fc5144bc6e39bdeedd27a2397cccf74/contents/packs/aws-sam/RULES.md] # AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model)

Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the AWS Serverless Application Model and the API-Gateway/CloudFront stack it deploys — true for any SAM project read cold.

- **esbuild must be a regular `dependency`, not a `devDependency`.** SAM's esbuild builder runs a *production-only* `npm install` in its scratch dir, so a `devDependency` esbuild is skipped and the build fails with "Cannot find esbuild." Declare it in `dependencies`, or put it on the runner's `PATH` before `sam build`.
- **CloudFront won't forward `Authorization` via a *custom* origin-request policy** — a custom `AWS::CloudFront::OriginRequestPolicy` listing `Authorization` is rejected at deploy ("The parameter Headers contains Authorization that is not allowed"). To forward it to the origin while keeping it out of the cache key (so public GETs share one cached entry), attach the **managed** `AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy (id `b689b0a8-53d0-40ab-baf2-68738e2966ac`) plus a custom cache policy that omits `Authorization`. Use the *ExceptHostHeader* variant specifically: forwarding the viewer `Host` to an API Gateway origin returns 403.
- **A deploy role must be able to drive the transform and CloudFront, or change-set creation fails with the real reason hidden.** The `Serverless-2016-10-31` transform runs as a macro, so the deploy principal needs `cloudformation:*`, and CloudFront management needs `cloudfront:*`, both at `Resource: "*"` (scope the *data-plane* grants to your stack instead). `sam deploy` surfaces only `Waiter ChangeSetCreateComplete failed` — the actual `AccessDenied` is visible only in the CloudFormation console's **Change sets** tab. Don't paper over it with `AdministratorAccess`.
- **A brand-new AWS account can't create a CloudFront distribution until AWS verifies it.** The deploy fails `AccessDenied: Your account must be verified before you can add new CloudFront resources` — an account-level anti-abuse gate, not an IAM or template bug. Open a Support case to get the account verified, and launch against the origin URL directly meanwhile.
- **A failed first `CREATE` must be cleaned up before you retry.** A stack left in `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE` (and a SAM managed-bucket stack stuck in `REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS`) can only be *deleted*, never updated. And any resource with `DeletionPolicy: Retain` survives the rollback orphaned, so the retry then fails `already exists` until you delete the orphan too.
- **API Gateway HTTP API (v2) rejects a `chrome-extension://` origin in CORS `AllowOrigins`** with `BadRequestException: Invalid format for origin`, accepting only `http(s)://…` or `*`. An API fronted by a browser-extension (or other non-`http`) origin must therefore set `AllowOrigins: ['*']` and rely on its **JWT authorizer**, not CORS, as the security boundary.
- **A CDN cache hit is served before the request reaches the origin or its authorizer**, so you cannot enforce request auth on a *cacheable* read without edge compute (Lambda@Edge) — and keying the cache per token destroys the hit rate that justified caching. Treat cacheable endpoints as public by design, and protect only uncached (write / per-user) paths at the authorizer.
- **Prefer a short CloudFront TTL over per-write cache invalidation.** Invalidation is billed per path beyond a small monthly free allowance, so a write-through design that invalidates on every write is a cost trap; a short TTL plus optimistic local rendering hides the propagation delay from the writer.
- **Bundle the AWS SDK into the Lambda artifact rather than relying on the managed runtime's copy.** The runtime doesn't ship every SDK sub-package (a missing one fails only at invoke), and its bundled SDK minor version drifts under you. Declare and bundle the SDK packages you import, and pin a non-EOL runtime explicitly rather than letting it float.
- **Review the change set before applying — `Replacement: True` on a stateful resource is a data-loss hard stop.** Replacement creates a *new, empty* resource; a DynamoDB table shows it whenever an immutable property (its `KeySchema`/`AttributeDefinitions`) changes. Enable stack **termination protection** too — it's a one-time CLI/API call (`update-termination-protection`), not expressible in the template body.
- **Adding a DynamoDB GSI does not backfill existing items.** The `UpdateTable` is additive and indexes only items that already carry the index's key attributes; rows written earlier stay invisible until each is rewritten with those attributes. Plan an explicit backfill pass if pre-existing data must appear in the new index.
- **A custom request header turns even a public GET into a preflighted CORS request.** Any non-simple header (e.g. a client-version header) makes the browser send an `OPTIONS` preflight, so the API's CORS `AllowHeaders` must list that header or the real request is blocked *in the browser* — while server-side unit tests that never run the CORS layer stay green.
- **Reach AWS from a session with the AWS CLI or a boto3 script — there is no AWS MCP tool.** A stack's real state comes from a CLI call (`aws cloudformation describe-stacks …`) — the last green deploy workflow only reports the last *deploy*, not the current stack state. The CLI is **not pre-installed on the cloud/web runner** (nor `boto3`/`sam`), so declare its install in the **environment setup script** (`pip install awscli`, or the official bundle) rather than per session; point it at the sandbox proxy's CA bundle (`AWS_CA_BUNDLE`) if a call fails TLS verification.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Claudinite/sha/3fd16f9d7fc5144bc6e39bdeedd27a2397cccf74/contents/packs/leaflet/RULES.md] # Leaflet

Portable, project-agnostic gotchas for the [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/) web-mapping library — loading it from a CDN, embedding a map in a page, and the marker/`divIcon` and plugin behaviours that bite regardless of which app renders the map. True for any Leaflet map read cold.

- **Feature-detect an optional Leaflet plugin before using it, and fall back to core when its CDN script didn't load.** A plugin's separate `<script>` (markercluster, heat, draw, …) can silently fail to load while the base Leaflet bundle succeeds, leaving `L.markerClusterGroup` (etc.) undefined. Guard the call with `typeof L.markerClusterGroup === "function"` and add markers straight to the map when it's absent — the base map must still render.

- **Default an embedded, mid-page map to `scrollWheelZoom: false` so it doesn't hijack the page scroll.** Construct it with `L.map(el, { scrollWheelZoom: false })`, or gate wheel-zoom behind a click/focus.

- **Keep the tile provider's attribution — it's a licence term, not decoration.** The `attribution: '… © OpenStreetMap contributors'` on the `L.tileLayer(...)` must stay even when tidying the UI. Set `maxZoom` to the provider's real ceiling (OSM tiles top out at 19) so Leaflet doesn't request zoom levels the provider doesn't serve.

- **When a marker needs its own CSS `transform`, put it on an inner element, not the `divIcon` root.** Leaflet positions every marker by writing an inline `transform: translate3d(...)` onto the icon's root element, clobbering any `transform` you set there on the next reposition. Make the icon root a zero-size anchor (`iconSize: [0, 0]`, `iconAnchor: [0, 0]`) and apply your rotation/centring transform to a `<span>` inside its `html`.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Claudinite/sha/3fd16f9d7fc5144bc6e39bdeedd27a2397cccf74/contents/packs/executable-requirements/RULES.md] # Executable requirements — the framework standard

The concrete conventions for running a numbered spec as tests — the mechanics only. The judgment
layer they implement — doc-first red-by-default, owner-owned expecteds, honest-gap tracking — is
not here, so a new project or a new stack adopts the framework by convention instead of
re-deriving it. Worked implementations: GoogleCalendarEventCreator (origin; extension/jsdom
rendering), TLDR (adds a cross-tier `server` kind), ShoutsAndWhispers (Flutter port; first `saga`
kind).

## 1. The layout is the contract

- Everything lives under **`dev/requirements/`**: `requirements.md` (the numbered prose spec),
  one **top-level folder per kind**, `shared/` for cross-kind infra, and the runners/gates. The
  spec file's path is the framework's structural fingerprint — this pack activates on it.
- **A requirement line** starts (optionally after a list dash) with a backtick-wrapped dotted
  number: `` `4.2` ``. A **leaf** is an id with no finer-numbered child. Parse with one shared
  regex (`` ^\s*(?:-\s+)?`(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)` ``) so specs stay drop-in compatible across projects.
- **The line is a scannable one-liner; expanded detail collapses.** A leaf in `requirements.md`
  reads as a single line the owner skims down the numbered spine on GitHub. Any expansion —
  rationale, acceptance notes, edge cases, the owner-verification recipe — lives inside a
  collapsed `<details>` block under the line, hidden until the owner expands it. The doc reviews
  as a clean spec, not walls of prose; the depth is one click away when wanted, invisible when
  not.
- **The folder is the kind.** A case's kind is the directory it lives in; the case declares no
  kind field. Cases are
  `<kind>/cases/<slug>.<leaf-id>.case.<ext>`: a stable feature slug (so retitling a spec section
  never forces renames), then the dotted leaf id.
- **Artifact expecteds live beside their case** (`<slug>.<id>.png`, `expected/<name>.json`);
  failure artifacts (actual/diff renders) go to a gitignored dir, never beside the goldens.
- Where the language discovers cases dynamically (Node `require`), the registry walks the
  folders; where it cannot (Dart/Flutter), each kind keeps a hand-written `manifest` and **the
  gate enforces manifest ⇄ disk equality** — an unregistered case file never runs, so unregistered
  must be red.

## 2. What the coverage gate checks

The bijection gate is one committed test. It must fail on every one of: a leaf no case claims
(doc-first red-by-default); a case claiming a non-existent leaf; two cases claiming one leaf; a misnamed case file; a kind directory absent from the registry (or a
registered kind with no directory); a manifest out of sync with disk (where manifests exist); an
image found in a coded kind's folder (a screenshot cannot verify a gesture or a pure rule); a
stray golden no case or step accounts for. Every rule iterates the registry — adding a kind never
edits the gate.

The gate checks repo state; an interactive feature run also has an *ordering*: after the
owner's feature-classified comment, an independent commit updating the spec (no code alongside)
precedes the first code commit on the branch. The spec's path defaults to the canonical
`dev/requirements/requirements.md`; a project whose spec lives elsewhere (a non-canonical
layout, or the pack pulled in via a `requires` from `spec-driven-product`) names it on the pack
entry as `config.spec`.

## 3. The kind vocabulary

Two forces pick a leaf's kind: what can **honestly observe** the assertion, and what gives the
**owner the simplest verification**. Prefer the kind whose expected is a **visual the owner checks
by sight** — a surface snapshot or a saga storyboard — and whose per-leaf test body is minimal:
drive to the state, capture, done, with the golden as the assertion rather than hand-written
expectations. Push as many requirements as can honestly be seen onto that visual path — the more
of the spec an owner verifies by *looking*, the more of it they actually review. Reserve the coded
kinds (behavior, logic) for what an image genuinely cannot see: a gesture's outgoing request, a
pure rule. Route each leaf to the kind that can actually see what it asserts:

- **surface snapshot** (`popup`, `icon`, `screen`, …): a rendered resting state, pixel-exact
  against a committed golden. One golden per leaf, even when several leaves render the same state
  — the bijection stays strict.
- **behavior**: a driven gesture and its outgoing request/consequence, asserted in code against
  the fakes' recordings. No images allowed in the folder.
- **logic**: a pure product rule, a coded `verify()` importing shipped code.
- **saga** (§4): a multi-step story as a golden storyboard.
- **per-project kinds** where the product's value is breadth or crosses tiers: a per-target
  `extractor`/`support` kind (one case per supported external target, proven on committed real
  samples), a `server` kind (the boundary's half of a two-tier rule, against the real handler).
- **heavy/e2e singleton**: "the product loads in the real environment" — one case, its own lane,
  never in the default loop.

## 4. Sagas: stories as storyboards

Single frames prove states; **sagas prove transitions and causality** — what arriving, acting, or
time passing *changes*. Use a saga when the requirement is the story ("a message sent before I
arrived never appears; one sent after I arrived does"), not decomposable into independent resting
states without losing the claim.

- A saga case is an ordered list of **steps**; each step = a caption plus an action against the
  fake world; after each step the runner captures one golden frame `<slug>.<id>.step-NN.png`.
- The **caption narrates the story** in user terms — captions surface in the gallery.
- One saga = one leaf; the frames are that one case's expected (all frames pixel-exact, same
  ownership rules as any golden). Keep sagas to 3–6 frames; a longer story is usually two sagas.
- Saga steps drive the **same real entry point** as every other kind (the shipped app shell/render
  function) — a saga must never become a scripted slideshow of hand-arranged states.

**Animated saga goldens** (recording the motion, not the frames). A per-step frame proves a resting
state; a saga can instead be **one animated golden** — an APNG per leaf — recording the real UI
*moving* between steps. What keeps it delay-free and deterministic:

- **Strip dead delay, keep the animation.** Render time is virtual, so a scripted wait is a run of
  *identical* frames — dedup consecutive identical frames and clamp any single hold, so the golden
  holds motion, never waiting (a 3 s wait must not become 3 s of golden).
- **Lossless, so byte-identity still holds.** Encode APNG, not GIF (whose palette and dithering
  aren't deterministic); the comparison stays exact byte-identity and a mismatch writes a per-frame
  `expected | actual | diff` to the gitignored failures dir. Capture at a low DPR — lossless costs
  no fidelity for it. Flutter reads each frame off the `RepaintBoundary` via `toImage` inside
  `runAsync` (the fake-async test zone won't otherwise complete the byte read).
- **Mark the gesture.** Paint an expanding ring at each real pointer gesture over the pre-reaction
  frame so the strip shows *where* the user acted; programmatic world changes draw none.

## 5. Determinism or it isn't spec

A rendered expected is only owner-ownable if it is byte-stable forever:

- **Pin the clock.** One shared reference time (`REFERENCE_NOW`) threaded to everything that
  formats or compares dates; fixture data is authored relative to it. Never wall-clock.
- **Fake every nondeterministic input**: network (map tiles, avatars — deterministic generated
  substitutes), randomness, platform sensors, locale (pin it; date copy is locale-sensitive),
  viewport (one fixed logical size and pixel ratio).
- **Load real fonts** in the render harness — test environments default to a glyph-less stub that
  renders text as boxes. Load the product's bundled families plus the
  icon font; watch for styles that don't inherit the family (button text styles are the classic
  leak) — pin the family there explicitly.
- **Never wait for "settled".** Indeterminate spinners animate forever; use fixed-duration pumps
  so an in-flight state is a capturable, deterministic frame.

## 6. Rendering recipes per stack

- **Browser-extension / DOM products** (the origin recipe): feed the case's fake data to the real
  `render()` in a jsdom document seeded from the real HTML, fold the real CSS on as inline styles,
  rasterize with satori + resvg, compare with pixelmatch at **zero tolerated diff ratio**. No real
  browser: deterministic and dependency-light, at a documented fidelity tradeoff.
- **Flutter**: widget-test golden files are the native equivalent — pump the real app shell
  against the fake world and `matchesGoldenFile`; `--update-goldens` is the refresh lane. Load
  fonts from the FontManifest (icons included). The fake world (scripted location/auth/backend
  that also *records* what the UI asked) is the product's own testing library so the requirements
  package and unit tests share it.
- Whatever the stack: the comparison is **pixel-exact**. A tolerance is a standing invitation for
  unreviewed drift; if a platform renders unstably, fix the determinism (fonts, clock, fakes), not
  the threshold.

## 7. The gallery is derived output

- The spec doubles as a visual gallery: under every image-kind leaf, machine-managed image lines
  (tagged with an HTML comment marker) embed the committed goldens — saga leaves get their full
  captioned storyboard strip.
- A committed **gallery gate** keeps the doc equal to the generator's output byte-for-byte.
  Regenerate via the tool, never by hand.

## 8. Refresh is a review step

One committed refresh entry point regenerates all goldens **and** the gallery together, so they
cannot skew. Running it is how an *intended* UI change lands — the refreshed PNGs ride the diff
for the owner to approve. It is never how a red case gets fixed: the re-baselining approval
procedure (surface actual/expected/diff, ask, only then re-baseline) is canon in the
writing-tests skill and the spec-driven-product playbook.

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Claudinite/sha/3fd16f9d7fc5144bc6e39bdeedd27a2397cccf74/contents/packs/flutter/RULES.md] # Flutter

Portable, project-agnostic practices for Flutter / Dart codebases — true for any Flutter project
read cold. Earned in missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers (a Firebase-backed, location-driven app with an
executable-requirements UI suite); keep anything project-specific in the consuming repo's docs.

## Architecture: ports out of the widget tree

- **Widgets depend on ports, never on plugins.** Every platform/backend concern (location, auth,
  push, backend calls, the clock) enters the UI as a hand-written abstract interface with pure-Dart
  value types; plugin adapters (`geolocator`, `firebase_*`, `google_sign_in`, …) implement them and
  are constructed **only** in `main.dart`. A plugin type leaking into a screen (a geolocator
  `Position`, a `FirebaseFunctionsException`) is a defect: it silently couples every widget test to
  the plugin's platform channels.
- **Enforce the boundary with a committed import-scan test** (dart:io over `lib/ui/`, `lib/screens/`
  looking for forbidden import prefixes). The analyzer won't stop a convenient leak.
- **Ship the fakes in the package** (`lib/testing/`): scripted fakes for each port that also
  *record* what the UI asked of them, plus a `FakeWorld` bundling them with a pinned clock and the
  real app shell. Both the app's own tests and any sibling test package (e.g. an
  executable-requirements suite) import one fake world — never two parallel ones.
- **Extract the root shell into a widget** (`lib/app.dart`) taking the ports as parameters, used
  identically by `main.dart` (adapters) and the test harness (fakes). Tests must never rebuild a
  parallel MaterialApp — actuals come from the shipped shell.
- **Inject the clock.** Any widget that formats or compares times takes a `Clock` port; relative
  time rendered from `DateTime.now()` is untestable and drifts goldens.

## Widget tests and goldens

- **Load real fonts before any golden** — the test binding defaults to the glyph-less Ahem stub
  (text renders as boxes). Parse `FontManifest.json` from the root bundle and `FontLoader` every
  family (strip the `packages/<pkg>/` prefix so plain family names resolve), which also loads
  MaterialIcons; bundle text faces (e.g. Roboto) in the test package's pubspec. Watch for styles
  that don't inherit the theme's family — `ButtonStyle`/`styleFrom` text styles are the classic
  leak; pin `fontFamily` there explicitly.
- **Never `pumpAndSettle` around indeterminate progress indicators** — they schedule frames
  forever and the call never returns. Use fixed-duration pumps (`pump()` then
  `pump(Duration(...))`); this also makes an in-flight state (a spinner mid-send) a deterministic,
  golden-capturable frame. Corollary: after `tap()`, pump **twice** — one frame applies state, the
  fixed-duration pump advances implicit animations (ink ripples, color lerps) past the capture.
- **Anything that fetches must be injectable**: map tile providers, avatar images. Widget tests
  block real HTTP (a 400-returning stub client), so a `NetworkImage`/network `TileProvider` in the
  tree means error boxes, not screenshots. Provide a deterministic in-memory substitute (a
  canvas-drawn `ImageProvider` works and needs no asset files).
- **Fix the viewport per suite**: set `tester.view.physicalSize` and `devicePixelRatio` to one
  phone-shaped size (and reset in teardown) so layout — and therefore goldens — can't drift with
  the harness default.
- **Async lifecycle guards need an epoch counter.** A `start()` that awaits (permission check,
  first fix) can re-arm streams/timers after `stop()`/dispose ran mid-await; bump an epoch in
  `stop()` and bail after every await if it changed. The symptom (leaked GPS subscription after
  sign-out) is invisible in tests that don't await realistically.

## Toolchain habits

- **Verify plugin APIs against the installed source, not memory.** Major Flutter plugins break
  their APIs often (google_sign_in v7's `authenticate()`, flutter_map v7+'s options, geolocator's
  settings objects); resolved versions live in the pub cache
  (`~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/<pkg>-<ver>/lib/`) — read them before writing against them.
- **`pubspec.lock` moving without `pubspec.yaml` moving is version skew, not a dependency change.**
  An app commits its lockfile (only a *library* package gitignores it), so the file is tracked on
  purpose — the thing to keep out of the diff is the churn a local `flutter pub get` produces when
  the installed SDK resolves differently from CI's. Unless you deliberately ran an upgrade, revert
  it: `git checkout -- pubspec.lock`.
- **`flutter analyze` at zero issues** (infos included) is the bar a suite holds; lints that fight
  a deliberate convention (e.g. `file_names` vs. leaf-id case filenames) get disabled narrowly in
  that package's `analysis_options.yaml` with the reason as a comment.
- **Sandboxed/CI runners**: `flutter test` can stall for minutes at teardown on GPU-less containers
  with dropped sockets. The pattern that holds: stream output, kill the process group the moment
  the definitive marker prints (`All tests passed!` / `Some tests failed`), watchdog-kill on output
  silence. On healthy machines plain `flutter test` is equivalent — keep the wrapper thin.
- **The web sandbox ships no Flutter SDK.** Claude Code on the web boots without Flutter, so tests,
  `flutter analyze`, and golden regen can't run until it's installed. Install belongs in the
  environment **image** (built once, snapshotted, reused) — never a per-session hook that reinstalls
  every start. This pack declares that need in its `env` block ([pack.mjs](pack.mjs)); a project pastes
  one generic `environment-setup-command.sh` that runs every active pack's requirement via
  [engine/pack_loader/env-requirements.mjs](../../engine/pack_loader/env-requirements.mjs) and asserts it at session start (see [bootstrap.md](../../bootstrap.md)
  Part 9).
